questions.question: In which language was 'Mudraraksha' play written by Vishakhadatta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Mudraraksha'** is a historical Sanskrit play written by **Vishakhadatta**.
 
• The play is believed to have been written between the **4th and 8th centuries CE**.
 
• It depicts the political and administrative strategies employed during the reign of the **Mauryan Empire**, particularly around the time of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• The narrative revolves around the clever diplomacy of **Chanakya (Kautilya)** to dethrone the Nanda dynasty and establish Chandragupta Maurya as the ruler.
 
• 'Mudraraksha' translates to "The Signet Ring of Rakshasa," referring to the role of Rakshasa, the loyal minister of the Nanda dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanskrit Literature:**

 
 
• Sanskrit is one of the oldest languages in the world and forms the basis of classical Indian literature.
 
• It has a rich tradition of plays, poetry, epics, and philosophical texts like the Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya:**
 
 
• Also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, he was a celebrated strategist and the author of the treatise **Arthashastra**.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of 'Mudraraksha':**
 
 
• The play provides insight into the political dynamics and strategies used during ancient Indian history.
 
• It highlights themes of loyalty, power, and statecraft.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE) was one of the largest empires in ancient India, founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• It reached its peak under Emperor Ashoka, known for his propagation of Buddhism and the Edicts of Ashoka.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote a book called 'Indica' based on his travels and experiences in Mauryan India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Megasthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Megasthenes** was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator to the Mauryan court of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya in the 4th century BCE.
 
• He authored the book **'Indica'**, which provides a detailed account of Mauryan India, including its geography, society, economy, and governance.
 
• The work of Megasthenes is considered one of the earliest known written accounts of India by a foreign traveler, offering valuable historical insights.
 
• 'Indica' has not survived in its entirety, but fragments and references to it are found in the writings of later authors like Strabo, Arrian, and Diodorus.
 
• His observations on the Mauryan administration, the caste system, and the city of Pataliputra are particularly notable for historians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indica and Its Legacy:**

 
 
• 'Indica' was a pioneering ethnographic work that provided a foreign perspective on ancient India.
 
• Although the original text is lost, its content has been preserved through citations by later Greek and Roman historians.
 
 
 
• **Megasthenes' Contributions:**
 
 
• He described the administrative efficiency of the Mauryan Empire under Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• His account includes details about Pataliputra (modern-day Patna), the empire's capital, which he compared to the grandeur of cities like Susa and Babylon.
 
 
 
• **Relations Between Greece and Mauryan India:**
 
 
• Megasthenes' visit highlights the diplomatic ties between the Mauryan Empire and the Hellenistic world following Alexander the Great's campaigns.
 
• Seleucus I Nicator, a Hellenistic ruler, sent Megasthenes to Chandragupta's court as part of a treaty agreement.
 
 
 
• **Other Ancient Travelers to India:**
 
 
• Other notable foreign accounts of ancient India include those by Fa-Hien, Hiuen Tsang, and Al-Biruni, who provided rich insights into Indian culture and history.

questions.question: The author of 'Arthashastra' was a contemporary of which of the following rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Arthashastra' was authored by **Chanakya**, also known as Kautilya.
 
• Chanakya served as the chief advisor to **Chandragupta Maurya**, the founder of the Maurya Empire.
 
• The period of **Chandragupta Maurya** was around 321-297 BCE.
 
• Chanakya played a crucial role in the establishment and consolidation of the Maurya Empire under Chandragupta Maurya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthashastra**:

 
 
• It is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• The text is attributed to Chanakya (Kautilya), who was a teacher at Takshashila and later became the prime minister of Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The treatise is divided into 15 books, dealing with various aspects of governance.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya**:
 
 
• He was an ancient Indian philosopher, economist, jurist, and royal advisor.
 
• Chanakya is often credited with being the architect of Chandragupta Maurya's rise to power and the establishment of the Maurya Empire.
 
• He is considered one of the greatest political strategists and thinkers in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Maurya Empire**:
 
 
• It was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE.
 
• It is one of the largest and most powerful empires in ancient India.
 
• The empire included a vast territory covering most of the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Takshashila**:
 
 
• An ancient center of learning located in modern-day Pakistan.
 
• Chanakya was associated with Takshashila as a teacher before becoming involved in politics.

questions.question: The famous Sanskrit grammar book 'Mahabhasya' was written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Patanjali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahabhasya** is a commentary on Panini's grammar work **Ashtadhyayi**.
 
• It was written by the Sanskrit grammarian **Patanjali**, who is also believed to have lived around the 2nd century BCE.
 
• The **Mahabhasya** is considered one of the most significant works in the field of **Sanskrit grammar** and linguistics.
 
• This work not only explains Panini's rules but also provides **critical analysis, examples, and counterexamples** to clarify grammatical concepts.
 
• It is one of the three foundational works of Sanskrit grammar, along with **Panini's Ashtadhyayi** and **Katyayana's Varttikas**.
 
• The **Mahabhasya** played an essential role in preserving the structure of the Sanskrit language and influenced later grammatical traditions.
 
• Patanjali is also often associated with the **Yoga Sutras**, although the authorship of both works by the same person is debated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhartruhari**__

 __
 
• **Bhartruhari** was an Indian linguist, poet, and philosopher who lived during the **5th century CE**.
 
• He is well-known for his work on language and grammar, particularly the **Vakyapadiya**, which deals with the **philosophy of language**.
 
• The Vakyapadiya discusses the relationship between language, thought, and reality.
 
 
 
• **Vedvyas**__
 __
 
• **Vedvyas** is a central figure in Indian mythology, credited with composing the **Mahabharata**.
 
• He is also believed to have compiled the **Vedas** and written the **Puranas**.
 
• However, there is no evidence linking him to works on grammar.
 
 
 
• **Panini**__
 
 
• **Panini** was a renowned Sanskrit grammarian who lived during the **5th–4th century BCE**.
 
• He is best known for his work **Ashtadhyayi**, a treatise that systematized Sanskrit grammar.
 
• Panini laid the foundation for the grammatical tradition, which was later expanded by Patanjali in the **Mahabhasya**.

questions.question: Which of the following was authored by Harisenacharya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihatkatha Kosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brihatkatha Kosh** was authored by Harisenacharya.
 
• The work is significant in the genre of Sanskrit literature.
 
• It is considered one of the important texts in classical Indian narratives.
 
• Harisenacharya's contribution through this work provides insights into the cultural and social aspects of his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajatarangini**

 
 
• Authored by Kalhana, it is a historical chronicle of the north-western Indian subcontinent, particularly the kings of Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Brihat Katha Manjari**
 
 
• Written by Kshemendra, it is an abridged version of the Brihatkatha, a large collection of stories attributed to Gunadhya.
 
 
 
• **Lilavati**
 
 
• A treatise on mathematics written by the Indian mathematician Bhaskara II, which deals with arithmetic, algebra, and geometry.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit Literature**
 
 
• Is one of the oldest literatures in the world, consisting of a vast body of texts in the Sanskrit language.
 
• Includes a wide range of works such as epics, hymns, philosophical treatises, poetry, drama, and scientific texts.
 
• Important texts include the Vedas, Upanishads, Mahabharata, Ramayana, and various other Shastras.

questions.question: "Arthashastra" was written by ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chanakya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Arthashastra

 
 
• The Arthashastra is one of the earliest works of political realism to have been written, along with Sun Tzu's The Art of War and Machiavelli's The Prince.
 
• The 'Arthashastra' is a treasure of Political Philosophy. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
 
• It is considered the most comprehensive treatise on statecraft of classical times.
 
• The first-ever book written on Practice of Management, this treatise is also about foreign policy, administration, economic reforms, policies, and war.
 
• It is a primeval Indian discourse on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy. 
 
• It is written in Sanskrit. 
 
• Kautilya's Arthasashtra was composed between the 3rd to 2nd Century B.C.
 
• It is mainly a work on the art of government.
 
• In his view, for the smooth functioning of administration and the welfare of the people, the king had to be acquainted with the four Vedas and four sciences of government (Anvikashaki, Trai, Varta, and Dandniti). 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Kautilya's administrative and judicial structure was hierarchical.
 
• He emphasized the principle of equity.
 
• He believed that law was an imperial command enforced by sanctions.
 
• He was both a thinker and statesman.
 
• He contributed to the formulation of some general principles capable of universal application and effectiveness in all times and ages.
 
• Arthsashtra sets the conceptual groundwork for making India the first welfare state.
 
• In Indian theory, State was usually thought to cover seven elements:
 
 
• The king
 
• The ministers
 
• The populace
 
• The fort
 
• The treasury
 
• The army
 
• The ally

questions.question: ‘Harshacharita’ (The Deeds of Harsha), which is the biography of Indian Emperor Harsha, was written by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Banabhatta.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Harshacharita is a biography of Harshavardhana, the ruler of Kannauj, composed in Sanskrit by his court poet, Banabhatta**.
 
• Harsha is known mainly through the works of** Banabhatta named Harsacharita ("Deeds of Harsha").**
 
• The work depicts the court and times of the Buddhist emperor Harsha of northern India.
 
• Bana's biography of Harsha provides valuable information about the period, though with some exaggeration in the emperor's favour.
 
• Written in the ornate kavya style, involving extremely lengthy constructions, elaborate descriptions, and poetic devices, the work has great vitality and a wealth of keenly observed detail.
 
• Himself a poet, Harsha composed three Sanskrit works:** Nagananda, Ratnavali, and Priyadarsika.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:**

 
 
• ​A signed hardcover copy of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore's 'The King of the Dark Chamber' - the English translation of his famous Bengali play 'Raja' - has been sold for USD 700 at an auction in the US.
 
• The play revolves around a mysterious, unseen, omniscient king, who is both benevolent and efficient. Tagore became the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize (Literature) in 1913.

questions.question: Who among the following scholars gave reference to the history of Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalhana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kalhana was a 12th-century Kashmiri poet and historian known for writing the **Rajatarangini**.
 
• The **Rajatarangini** is a historical chronicle of early Kashmir and is considered one of the earliest historical records of the region.
 
• Kalhana's work is highly regarded for its detailed account of the history, culture, and geography of Kashmir.
 
• The **Rajatarangini** covers the history of Kashmir from its mythical origins to the 12th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalhana's Life**

 
 
• Kalhana was the son of a minister named Champaka in the Kashmiri court.
 
• He lived during the reign of King Harsha of Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Rajatarangini**
 
 
• Rajatarangini means "River of Kings" in Sanskrit.
 
• The text is composed of eight books called "Tarangas" (waves), each detailing a different period of Kashmiri history.
 
• The work is written in Sanskrit and is considered a crucial source for understanding ancient and medieval Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• Rajatarangini provides insights into the political, social, and cultural aspects of Kashmiri society.
 
• It is one of the few historical texts from medieval India that attempts to present a chronological account of events.
 
 
 
• **Influence on Historiography**
 
 
• Kalhana's methodology in compiling historical data set a precedent for future historians.
 
• His critical approach to sources and emphasis on chronology were innovative for his time.
